detailed_description: Text Statistics counts characters, characters without spaces, words, sentences, paragraphs, lines, unique words, digits, spaces, estimated reading time, estimated speaking time, and average word length. Paste text and the page updates the measurements so writers, editors, students, and marketers can quickly inspect length and structure. The estimates use simple text rules and should be treated as guidance, especially for languages or content styles where word boundaries and sentence punctuation differ.
usage_steps: Paste or type text into the input area.
Review the character and word counts.
Check sentence, paragraph, and line counts.
Use reading and speaking time estimates for planning.
Revise the text and watch the numbers update.
Copy or record the metrics you need.
usage_examples: Check whether a meta description draft is too long.
Estimate reading time for an article excerpt.
Count words in an assignment paragraph.
Compare unique word count before and after editing.

faqs.question: What does it count?
faqs.answer: It counts characters, words, sentences, paragraphs, lines, unique words, digits, spaces, and timing estimates.

faqs.question: Are reading time estimates exact?
faqs.answer: No. They are simple estimates based on typical reading speed.

faqs.question: Does it work for every language equally?
faqs.answer: Counts may be less precise for languages without spaces or with different punctuation conventions.

faqs.question: Can I use it for SEO snippets?
faqs.answer: Yes. It is useful for checking draft lengths, but search engines may rewrite snippets.

faqs.question: Does it upload my text?
faqs.answer: The visible analysis runs in the browser page and does not require account login.
